narratives.Description: A green `verify:ac` with zero verified clauses still leads with "verify:ac passed (#3284)", so a fresh brief reads as done before any work exists. This story changes only that first line to "verify:ac: no acceptance evidence yet (#3284)" when no clause verified and no acceptance command ran green, keeps `ok`, the exit code and the resolution label, and keeps the two zero-verified refusals (rapid check #4866, scope:complete #4870) exactly as they are by teaching their one detector the new line. It also adds a context-only note on verified rows whose file is unchanged since the commit before a committed brief entered its folder, and says in the verify:ac help text and the pre-PR skill that exit 0 means no clause failed.
narratives.UserStory: As a worker or reviewer reading `verify:ac`, I want the first line to say there is no acceptance evidence yet when nothing was verified, so that I do not read a brief with no evidence as done.
narratives.ImplementationPlan: One product PR (deft-story: 6374). 1. acceptance-resolver.ts: relabelVerifyAcPassLead takes whether any acceptance command ran green; with zero verified clauses and no green run the lead is "verify:ac: no acceptance evidence yet (#3284)" with the same counts, provenance and rung; the pass-line filter also drops the old lead. 2. evaluate.ts: labelVerdict passes the green-run fact; applyClauseWalk adds the context note to verified rows through the new verify-ac/entry-baseline-note.ts (git log --diff-filter=A for the brief at its path, parent commit, byte compare of each verified row's file; no note outside git, for an uncommitted brief or a terminal folder). 3. rapid-zero-verified.ts: the lead pattern accepts both lines. 4. tasks/verify.yml help text, the pre-PR skill (and its pack JSON), plan-acceptance.md and commands.md say exit 0 means no clause failed; evaluator-surface disposition for tasks/verify.yml. 5. Tests for every AC; changelog.d fragment. #6408 (pre-existing evidence) and #6257 (evidence stamping) are not absorbed.
narratives.Overview:
1. Zero-verified lead. When the result is green, no acceptance command ran green, and the walk verified zero clauses, the first line reads "verify:ac: no acceptance evidence yet (#3284)" with the same counts, in place of "verify:ac passed (#3284)". This applies on every branch and to every brief. In every other case the first line is as today.
2. `ok`, the exit code and the resolution label never change.
3. Existing refusals are preserved, not widened. The one detector `acceptanceWalkReportsZeroVerified` recognises the item 1 line as well as the old line, in quiet output too. Rapid `check` (#4866) and `scope:complete` (#4870) give the same result as today for every input.
4. Context note, with no bearing on any result. For a brief in a non-terminal lifecycle folder that is committed at its current path, a `verified` row whose bound file is identical in the working tree to its content at the parent of the commit that added the brief at that path prints "file unchanged since the commit before this brief entered this folder" in its detail. A brief that is not committed at its current path, a brief in a terminal folder and a checkout outside git get no note and no extra line.
5. Wording of the contract. The `verify:ac` help text and the pre-PR skill say that exit 0 means no clause failed, not that the requested work exists.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a brief with zero verified clauses and no green acceptance command, when `task verify:ac` runs on a fresh branch with no commit, then the first line reads "no acceptance evidence yet".
- Given the same brief on the delivery branch, when `task verify:ac` runs, then the first line reads "no acceptance evidence yet".
- Given either run, then the exit code is the same as today.
- Given a result with zero verified clauses under the new first line, when rapid `task check` reads it, then rapid `check` exits 1 as today.
- Given that result with no executable pass, when `scope:complete` reads it, then `scope:complete` refuses as today.
- Given that result in quiet output, then the zero-verified detector still matches.
- Given a brief with at least one verified clause, when `task verify:ac` runs, then the first line is the same as today.
- Given a brief whose acceptance command ran green, when `task verify:ac` runs, then the first line says "passed" as today.
- Given an active brief that is committed at its path and a verified clause on a file unchanged since the commit before the brief entered `active/`, when `task verify:ac` runs, then that row carries the context note.
- Given an active brief that is not committed at its path, when `task verify:ac` runs, then no row carries the note.
- Given any run, then the note does not change the first line or the exit code.

## In plain English
`verify:ac` checks a brief's acceptance clauses against the files the brief names. A fresh brief can pass before the worker has changed anything. Two things cause that. First, a clause the tool cannot judge is reported as "unverifiable" and does not count against the result, and the first line of the output still says "verify:ac passed". Second, a clause can come back "verified" from a file that already existed before the work: the clause says a file exists, or names a text that is already in the file. The issue asks that a green result is not read as proof that the work exists, and prefers a change to what the result says over a new refusal. The open question is whether wording alone is enough, because other tools read the exit code and not the words.

## Pains
- P1 — When no clause was verified, the output still leads with "verify:ac passed", so a reader takes a brief with no evidence as done.
- P2 — A clause can be reported "verified" from a bound file that is unchanged from the merge base, so evidence that existed before the work counts as evidence of the work.

## Out of this arc
- Evidence stamping that treats a file binding as proof (#6257). That is the neighbouring problem at completion. This arc covers the `verify:ac` result only and does not absorb #6257.
- Any change to which clauses ingest writes (#6333) or to artifact binding at promote.

## Anchors at the dispatch SHA (claims, to be re-verified)
- `packages/core/src/verify-ac/clauses.ts` `walkOne` (1456-1622): an unbound clause, a clause outside the declared scope and a behavioral clause with no token or existence claim return `unverifiable` with `adjudicable: false`. An existence claim on a present file returns `verified` (1607-1609). Quoted tokens present in the file return `verified` (1604). The walk never compares the file with the merge base.
- Same file, `walkAcceptanceClauses` (1897-1924): `ok` is true when no clause failed and no adjudicable clause is unverified.
- `packages/core/src/product-first-done-gate/acceptance-resolver.ts` `relabelVerifyAcPassLead` (427-457): a green result leads with "verify:ac passed (#3284) (N verified, M unverifiable)". `clauseWalkBlocks` (478-492): unverifiable clauses with no oracle never block.
- `packages/core/src/product-first-done-gate/evaluate.ts` `applyClauseWalk` (1207-1247): an empty pass becomes `verified-pass` only when at least one clause verified.
- `packages/core/src/check/cached-orchestrator.ts` (855-873) and `check/rapid-zero-verified.ts`: rapid `check` already exits 1 when the walk verified zero clauses, without relabelling the `verify:ac` gate (#4866).

## Operator direction recorded for this arc
Prefer a design that removes steps over one that adds a gate. A new refusal needs a reason that no existing control covers. The issue itself prefers a change to what the result says.

## In plain English

A fresh brief can pass because its files already exist, even when its requested behavior has not been demonstrated. Clearer reporting would help, but **the refutation target does not hold as written**: changing words while keeping success unchanged cannot ensure that every consumer stops treating success as acceptance.

Ordinary pre-PR still accepts the exit status; non-rapid `check` can continue, and CI runs the merge-check path. Rapid `check` and `scope:complete` already have additional protections against zero verified clauses. Those protections parse the wording being changed, so this reporting change could accidentally disable them. These are acceptance-path conclusions, not a claim that every other completion or CI requirement would pass.

An unchanged file also does not necessarily mean “no evidence”: a test can demonstrate behavior without changing its own file. Conversely, an unrelated edit does not demonstrate the requested behavior.

### 1. blocks-the-design — Reporting alone does not change what success permits

**Evidence at `72fe1658a04cef37d4dbea2bdad46ca087721853`:**

- `packages/core/src/verify-ac/clauses.ts:1599–1622` credits token checks and file existence, while behavioral claims without an oracle remain non-adjudicable.
- `packages/core/src/verify-ac/clauses.ts:1898–1907` computes success from the absence of failures and unverified adjudicable clauses.
- `packages/core/src/product-first-done-gate/evaluate.ts:1232–1245` preserves success and can promote an empty pass to `verified-pass` when any clause verifies.
- `packages/core/src/check/cached-orchestrator.ts:718–728,823–838,855–873` handles nonzero exit status and adds the separate rapid zero-verified refusal.
- `content/skills/deft-directive-pre-pr/SKILL.md:224–226,271` requires the local acceptance run and refusal on exit 1.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml:201–202,503–504` runs `task check:merge`.

**Failure mode:** A brief with only unjudgeable behavioral clauses still returns success after its lead becomes “no evidence yet.” Pre-PR’s stated exit-status rule still admits that result. The rapid-only safeguard does not establish equivalent protection for other check modes. A reporting-only label also leaves existing structured success fields intact unless explicitly changed.

**Disposition consequence:** The universal consumer claim cannot bind. The smallest defensible scope is an honest reporting improvement that explicitly leaves acceptance policy unchanged. If preventing downstream acceptance is required, identify the existing consumer decisions that must change; do not claim prose alone provides that guarantee.

The strongest case for unchanged exit codes is compatibility: inability to judge a clause is not evidence that implementation failed. That supports the narrower reporting fix. It does not support the stronger assertion that green can no longer be mistaken for demonstrated work.

### 2. blocks-the-design — The proposed wording is already an input to refusal logic

**Evidence at the dispatch SHA:**

- `packages/core/src/check/rapid-zero-verified.ts:21–39` recognizes zero verification through two exact text patterns: the clause-walk summary and the current pass lead.
- The same file, `61–77,101–114`, uses that recognition for rapid-check refusal and completion refusal without an executable pass.
- `packages/core/src/scope/acceptance-evidence.ts:1941–1971` applies the completion safeguard.
- `packages/core/src/product-first-done-gate/evaluate.ts:1221` suppresses the clause-walk message in quiet mode.

**Failure mode:** Replacing the pass lead and changing the summary to include a new outcome can leave neither pattern matching. Quiet output makes the pass-lead dependency especially relevant. A run that previously triggered an existing refusal can then escape it, despite the `verify:ac` exit code remaining unchanged.

**Disposition consequence:** Consumer compatibility must be part of this design, not an incidental implementation detail. Preserve the existing zero-verification decision through the new reporting format, including quiet output and the existing executable-pass exception. Reuse the existing safeguards; this finding does not require another gate.

### 3. sharpens-framing — File changes measure novelty, not evidence

**Evidence at the dispatch SHA:**

- `packages/core/src/verify-ac/clauses.ts:1584–1609` judges current token contents or existence, without proving that a relevant change introduced them.
- `packages/core/src/product-first-done-gate/acceptance-resolver.ts:479–492` explicitly distinguishes a green executable run from static clause adjudication.
- `packages/core/src/product-first-done-gate/evaluate.ts:1225–1230` supplies executable-run success separately from the bound-file walk.

**Failure mode:** An unchanged test file can pass against newly implemented behavior elsewhere. Calling that clause “no evidence yet” solely because its bound file is unchanged contradicts the existing executable-evidence path and the issue’s requirement to preserve test-verified results. In the other direction, adding an unrelated comment to an existing file makes it changed while leaving the old existence/token evidence equally weak.

**Disposition consequence:** Keep baseline change information separate from verification strength. “Bound file unchanged from baseline” is supportable; “no evidence yet” requires checking the available oracle evidence. A changed file must not, by itself, upgrade the result to proof that requested work exists. This clarification allows a reporting-focused remedy without absorbing evidence stamping from #6257.

## In plain English
Problem: `verify:ac` can be green before any work exists. A clause the tool cannot judge does not count against the result, and a clause can come back "verified" from a file that already existed before the work. The first line of the output still says "verify:ac passed".

What the critic found: wording alone cannot stop every tool from treating a green exit as done. Pre-PR, non-rapid `check` and CI read the exit code. Two existing protections (rapid `check` and `scope:complete`) already refuse a result with zero verified clauses, and they find that result by matching the exact words this change would edit, so a careless wording change would switch them off. The critic also showed that "the file did not change" is not the same as "no evidence": an unchanged test file can pass against new behaviour elsewhere, and an unrelated edit to a file proves nothing.

Solution this lean proposes: say less than "passed" when there is nothing new behind the result, and change nothing about who is refused. On a work branch, `verify:ac` notes for each verified clause whether its file differs from the merge base. When no acceptance command ran green and no verified clause sits on a changed file, the first line says "no new acceptance evidence yet" in place of "passed". The exit code stays the same. The two existing protections keep firing on exactly the results they fire on today.

What this adds: no gate, refusal, approval or stop. One read of the branch's changed-file list per run, one changed first line, and one note on some rows.

What it does not do: pre-PR, non-rapid `check` and CI still treat exit 0 as success. This design makes the result honest for a person or agent who reads it; it does not make those tools stricter. It does not touch evidence stamping at completion (#6257). If confirmed, the synthesis would assert this design. There is no leftover next-build.

## Bound remedy
1. Baseline fact. When the branch HEAD differs from its merge base with the delivery branch, the clause walk records, for each clause bound to a declared file, whether that file differs from the merge base (committed, staged, unstaged or untracked). When the merge base cannot be resolved or equals HEAD, no baseline fact is recorded and the output is as today.
2. Row note. A `verified` row whose file is unchanged from the merge base prints "file unchanged from the merge base" in its detail. Its outcome and its weight in the result do not change.
3. Lead line. When the result is green, no acceptance command ran green, and no `verified` row is on a changed file, the first line reads "verify:ac: no new acceptance evidence yet (#3284)" with the same counts, in place of "verify:ac passed (#3284)". In every other green case the first line is as today. `ok` and the exit code do not change.

6. Wording of the contract. The `verify:ac` help text and the pre-PR skill say that exit 0 means no clause failed, not that the requested work exists.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Given a work branch and a brief whose clauses are all bound to files unchanged from the merge base, when `task verify:ac` runs and no acceptance command ran green, then the first line reads "no new acceptance evidence yet".
- Given that run, then the exit code is the same as today.
- Given that run, then each `verified` row on an unchanged file says that the file is unchanged from the merge base.
- Given that run, then each `unverifiable` row is listed as today.
- Given a brief with at least one `verified` clause on a file changed from the merge base, when `task verify:ac` runs, then the output is the same as today.
- Given a brief whose acceptance command ran green, when `task verify:ac` runs, then the first line says "passed" as today.
- Given a checkout where HEAD equals the merge base, when `task verify:ac` runs, then the output is the same as today.
- Given a result with zero verified clauses under the new first line, when rapid `task check` reads it, then rapid `check` exits 1 as today.
- Given that result with no executable pass, when `scope:complete` reads it, then `scope:complete` refuses as today.
- Given that result in quiet output, then the zero-verified detector still matches.
- Given an unchanged test file and a green acceptance command, when `task verify:ac` runs, then the result is not reported as lacking evidence.

- Changing the exit code of `verify:ac` for a result with unverifiable clauses. That reverses #3826 and adds a refusal.
- Downgrading a `verified` row to another outcome because its file is unchanged (comment 6908107575 finding 3).
- Treating a changed file as proof that the requested work exists (comment 6908107575 finding 3).
